headline: Why is My Fence Post Wobbly?
articleBody: A wobbly fence post is more than just annoying; it's often a sign that something's not quite right with your fence's foundation. It can lead to panels coming loose, gates sagging, and ultimately, a less secure and attractive yard. So, what makes a fence post start to wobble? One of the biggest culprits is soft or rotted wood at the base of the post, especially where it meets the ground. Over time, moisture and soil can really do a number on timber, weakening it significantly. Another common issue is that the post wasn't set deep enough to begin with, or the material used to secure it (like concrete or gravel) has degraded or shifted. Repeated movement from wind, or even from gates swinging, can also loosen the fasteners or the ground around the post. If you notice your post leaning significantly, or if it feels really loose when you give it a shake, it might be time for a more substantial repair, perhaps even replacement. For situations where multiple posts are wobbly, or if it's a gate post, professional help can ensure the repair is done right and lasts.
